cities.base: Central Oslo, walkable to the harbor at Aker Brygge and a short tram or walk to Vigeland Park.
cities.name: Oslo

cities.base: Flåm village itself, right by the railway station and the fjord dock, there isn't really another option.
cities.name: Flåm

cities.base: Near Bryggen and the fish market, walkable to the Fløibanen funicular base station.
cities.name: Bergen

cities.base: Day trip only, the far end of the Nærøyfjord boat run from Flåm.
cities.name: Gudvangen

cities.base: Day trip only, a 20-minute drive from Flåm, needs a rental car.
cities.name: Stegastein Viewpoint

places.name: Bryggen
places.note: The wharf houses are the photo, the shops inside are mostly tourist stock, don't linger paying for anything there.

places.name: Bergen Cathedral (Domkirke)
places.note: Skip: modest interior, often closed for events, five minutes gets you the exterior which is the whole story.

places.name: Troldhaugen (Edvard Grieg's Home)
places.note: Grieg's villa and composing hut by the water, includes a small concert hall with occasional lunchtime recitals. Worth the bus trip if you care about the music, skip otherwise.

places.name: Lysøen (Ole Bull's Villa)
places.note: Composer's villa on its own island, ferry plus bus needed to get there, a half-day commitment. Skip unless you have a slow day and like 19th century eccentrics.

places.name: Fløyen summit trails (Blåmanen loop)
places.note: Once at the top of the funicular, a real forest trail loop, not just a viewing platform. Wear real shoes, it gets muddy.

places.name: St Mary's Church (Mariakirken)
places.note: Bergen's oldest building still in use, Romanesque, usually near empty compared to Bryggen outside.

places.name: Mount Ulriken (Ulriksbanen cable car)
places.note: Higher and quieter than Fløyen, better views on a clear day, but it's a bus ride out of the center so only worth it if Fløyen didn't satisfy you.

places.name: Fantoft Stave Church
places.note: A 1990s reconstruction after arson, not original, but the design itself is the real stave church form. Skip if you're already seeing one elsewhere in Norway.

places.name: KODE Art Museums
places.note: Four buildings around Lille Lungegårdsvannet, strong Munch holdings without the Oslo crowds. Good rainy-day option.

places.name: Fløibanen Funicular
places.note: Ride up is 6-8 min, the point is the trails and view at the top, budget 2-3 hours there not just the ride. Hours shorten in winter, confirm before you go.

places.name: Gudvangen Viking Village (Njardarheimr)
places.note: Reconstructed Viking-age settlement at the far end of the fjord where the Nærøyfjord boat lands, costumed staff and craft demonstrations. Sits well outside a Stegastein day trip logistically, better paired with the fjord cruise day if you have the car that day too, otherwise skip, it leans theatrical.

places.name: Hanseatic Museum and Schøtstuene
places.note: Original merchant's house interior, gives Bryggen's facades actual context, better than most of the shops next to it.

places.name: Fisketorget (Bergen Fish Market)
places.note: Go for dinner not lunch, tour groups thin out. Fish soup or seafood plate runs 150-250 NOK, some stalls overcharge tourists so check prices first.

places.name: Undredal Stave Church
places.note: From around 1147, one of the smallest stave churches still in regular use. Opening hours are limited and seasonal, check before making the drive out just for this.

places.name: Undredal
places.note: Tiny goat-farming village reachable by a tunnel off the Aurland road or by boat, known for brown goat cheese and Norway's smallest stave church (seats around 40). A further detour past Stegastein, only sensible if you have most of a day free with the car.

places.name: Flåm village and harbor walk
places.note: Where you're actually staying, so it's the fallback if Stegastein doesn't happen. Short walk along the harbor and up the valley road, pleasant but touristy near the cruise dock and railway station.

places.name: Otternes Bygdetun (farm settlement)
places.note: Cluster of around 30 wooden farm buildings, some dating to the 1700s, still privately owned, open for wandering. Sits above the fjord on the way between Flåm and Aurland, easy to combine with the Stegastein detour if driving.

places.name: Short hike, Stegastein platform surroundings
places.note: A short marked path leads a little further along the ridge from the parking area, giving a quieter angle on the fjord away from the platform crowds. Not a real trail, just a stretch of the leg.

places.name: Vangen Church (Aurland kyrkje)
places.note: Stone church from the 1200s, still in use, plain and small. Worth the ten minutes if you're already stopped in Aurland village, not a special trip on its own.

places.name: Aurland village
places.note: Small fjordside village on the way up to Stegastein, quieter than Flåm, a place to see actual working harbor life rather than cruise-ship shops. Not much to actively do beyond a short walk along the water.

places.name: Stegastein Viewpoint
places.note: Cantilevered platform 650m above Aurlandsfjord, about 30m out over the edge with a glass end panel. No barrier vertigo is real for some people. Needs a car, 20 minutes up a steep single-lane road from the Aurland turnoff off the Flåm-Voss road.

places.name: Kjelfossen waterfall viewing spot
places.note: One of Norway's taller waterfalls, visible from the road between Gudvangen and Stalheim, a quick stop rather than a hike if you have a car for that stretch.

places.name: Stalheim Hotel viewpoint terrace
places.note: Historic hotel above the Nærøydalen valley with a terrace open to non-guests for the view down the valley toward Gudvangen. Only realistic with a car, on the same road as Stalheimskleiva.

places.name: Gudvangen bus stop (Voss connection)
places.note: Functional stop only, this is where the bus to Voss picks up after the ferry docks, no reason to linger beyond catching the connection.

places.name: Nærøyfjord kayak tour from Gudvangen
places.note: Guided sea kayak trips onto the fjord run from operators based at Gudvangen. A slower and quieter way to see the same cliffs as the ferry, but it eats half a day and only makes sense if you are not also doing the full boat cruise the same day.

places.name: Staying overnight in Gudvangen
places.note: Skip. There is little reason to sleep here rather than in Flåm, the village exists for the fjord dock and the Viking village, both doable as a same-day stop with nights kept in Flåm as already planned.

places.name: Gudvangen Fjordtell cafe
places.note: Basic cafe attached to the small hotel by the dock, fine for a waffle or soup between boat and bus, not a destination meal.

places.name: Gudvangen dockside souvenir shops
places.note: Skip. A cluster of gift shops that appear whenever a cruise boat docks, troll dolls and overpriced knitwear, nothing distinct to the region.

places.name: Nærøydalen valley walk
places.note: The valley leading inland from Gudvangen has a flat gravel path good for a short walk while waiting for a bus connection, waterfalls visible from the road, nothing technical.

places.name: Stalheimskleiva road viewpoint
places.note: A steep hairpin road above Gudvangen with waterfalls on both sides, dramatic but needs a car or the bus route via Voss that passes it. Not reachable if you're doing the fjord as a straight there-and-back boat trip.

places.name: Njardarheimr Viking Village
places.note: A reconstructed Viking-age village with actors in character, built specifically for Gudvangen's tourist trade. Genuinely more elaborate than it sounds, but it is a themed attraction not a historic site, go in knowing that.

places.name: Gudvangen village and fjord dock
places.note: The village itself is tiny, a handful of buildings at the head of the Nærøyfjord. Most people pass through arriving or leaving by boat or bus, but the dock area with the fjord walls rising straight up is worth standing at for ten minutes even without a boat ticket.

places.name: Vigeland Park
places.note: Free, always open, the outdoor sculptures are the whole point so skip the attached museum unless you're a Vigeland completist.

places.name: Fram Museum
places.note: Better choice right now than the Viking Ship Museum, which has been partly closed for rebuilding, confirm current status before you go.

places.name: Aker Brygge
places.note: Harbor walk with restaurants, good for a low-key first evening after landing.

places.name: Flåm Railway
places.note: One of the steeper standard-gauge lines anywhere, buy one-way if you're continuing on to Gudvangen the next day.

places.name: Nærøyfjord cruise to Gudvangen
places.note: The real UNESCO fjord, don't let it get swapped for a generic Bergen-area harbor tour.

places.name: Stegastein Viewpoint
places.note: Needs a rental car, skip entirely if you're on public transit, a taxi out here isn't worth it.

places.name: Fløibanen funicular and Mount Fløyen
places.note: Round trip is 15 minutes but budget 2-3 hours up top for the trails, confirm current hours since they shorten in winter.

places.name: Fisketorget (Bergen fish market)
places.note: Go for dinner not lunch, it's calmer and the tour groups thin out.

places.name: Ægir BryggeriPub
places.note: Norse-longhouse-style microbrewery restaurant next to the station, good beer flight, sit-down dinner option that isn't just the tourist cafeteria by the dock.

places.name: Flåm village and church walk
places.note: Short loop past the small wooden Flåm Church (1670) and along the river, all there is to it once the cruise ships empty out, but pleasant and free.

places.name: Flåm harbor viewpoint
places.note: The dock end of the fjord arm, worth a few minutes for the mountain wall reflections, gets crowded when cruise ships are in port.

places.name: Kjosfossen waterfall stop
places.note: The train stops here for photos, includes a staged huldra dancer performance in summer. Corny but it is included in the ticket and everyone gets off.

places.name: Stegastein viewpoint
places.note: Cantilevered platform 650m above the fjord, free, but needs a car, about 20 minutes from Flåm. Skip if relying on public transit, no bus goes there.

places.name: Flåm Railway (Flåmsbana)
places.note: One of the steepest standard-gauge railways in the world, genuinely worth doing once. Buy one-way if continuing on to Gudvangen the next day, the round trip is wasted money otherwise.

places.name: Gudvangen
places.note: The far end of the fjord cruise, a handful of buildings and a reconstructed Viking longhouse market (Njardarheimr) that's more elaborate than it sounds if you have spare time before the bus back.

places.name: Otternes Bygdetun
places.note: Cluster of preserved 18th and 19th century farm buildings on a hillside a few km from Flåm, free to wander, quiet, no crowds, doable by rental car or a longer walk.

places.name: Flåm Camping og Vandrarheim café
places.note: Simple, cheap sandwiches and waffles, useful for a low-key lunch away from the cruise-ship-priced places right at the dock.

places.name: Heimly Pensjonat waterfront
places.note: Small guesthouse restaurant right on the water a short walk from the main dock, quieter than the tour-group cafeteria, decent fish dinner.

places.name: Fretheim Hotel restaurant
places.note: The historic hotel in the village, sit-down dinner with fjord views, the best formal option in Flåm itself, priced accordingly and can feel like the whole cruise crowd had the same idea.

places.name: Bryggen
places.note: Wharf houses are the photo, the shop interiors are tourist stock, don't linger paying for anything inside.

outings.why: Free open-air sculpture park, 1.5-2 hours, the sculptures outside are the whole point, skip the attached museum unless you love Vigeland specifically.
outings.name: Vigeland Park

outings.why: Polar exploration museum, 1.5 hours, better bet right now than the Viking Ship Museum which has been partly closed for rebuilding, confirm before you go.
outings.name: Fram Museum

outings.why: Regular train Oslo to Myrdal (about 5 hrs) then the Flåm Railway down (1 hr), one of the steeper standard-gauge lines anywhere, genuinely worth doing once, buy one-way not round trip if continuing on to Gudvangen.
outings.name: Flåm Railway to Myrdal connection

outings.why: The real UNESCO fjord by boat, about 2 hours one-way, roughly 5 hours door to door with the return leg, don't let this get downgraded to a generic Bergen-area harbor tour.
outings.name: Nærøyfjord boat to Gudvangen
outings.fallback: Stay in Flåm village and walk the shoreline if weather or booking falls through.

outings.why: A cliff-edge viewing platform above the fjord, free, but needs a rental car, skip entirely if relying on public transit since a taxi isn't worth it.
outings.name: Stegastein viewpoint drive
outings.season: late spring to autumn, road conditions permitting

outings.why: Bus and train combination through Voss, about 3.5-4 hours, arrives Bergen in time for an afternoon walk on Bryggen.
outings.name: Flåm to Bergen via Voss

outings.why: Funicular round trip is 15 minutes but budget 2-3 hours up top for the trails and view, build slack in since Bergen's weather is unreliable.
outings.name: Mount Fløyen via Fløibanen
outings.fallback: Wander Bryggen and the covered fish market stalls instead if it's pouring.

destination.name: Norway: Oslo, Sognefjord & Bergen
destination.pitch: A spine of Oslo, the real Nærøyfjord out of Flåm, and Bergen, built around real nights in the fjord rather than a Bergen day trip pretending to be one.
destination.caveat: Norway is expensive enough to surprise people who think they've priced Western Europe before, and Bergen's weather can flatten your one clear-sky day. Put together for you just now from what I know, rather than checked against today's opening times. Worth confirming anything you're pinning the trip on.

because.city: Oslo and Bergen both give you a real evening-harbor-walk city fix without needing a full extra day.
because.food: Bergen's Fisketorget for a calm evening fish soup once the tour groups thin out.
because.nature: The Nærøyfjord out of Flåm is the actual UNESCO fjord, not a generic harbor cruise near Bergen.
because.culture: The Fram Museum in Oslo covers polar exploration properly in 1.5 hours.
because.adventure: Stegastein viewpoint if you've got a car, a cliff-edge platform above the fjord.
because.exploration: The Flåm Railway itself is one of the steepest standard-gauge lines anywhere and worth riding once.
